clue.text: Malodorous mineral big momma takes one to see

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: the word for momma takes another piece into its middle, holding it

parts.note: mum is a mother, a homely version of momma
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A matriarch acquires a smelly rock specimen to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' puts I inside MUM, giving MIUM, after OS. 'Malodorous' is fair: the metal's name comes from the Greek for smell, from its pungent oxide.
explanation.definitionFit: The element's name derives from Greek osme, smell, because its oxide has a sharp odour, and it is mined as a natural metal.

clue.text: Voltaire's novel, frank and finally true

parts.note: frank and candid both mean open and honest

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word true

explanation.surface: Praise for Voltaire's book as honest and, in the end, truthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E, the last letter of 'true'.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's satirical 1759 tale follows a naive young man taught that all is for the best.

clue.text: As a whole, neutral, but one Frenchman is prejudiced

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, a French gentleman
partial means biased, favouring one side

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be even-handed while admitting a bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a whole' tells you to run the pieces together into one word; read apart they say 'I'm partial', the opposite of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone neutral takes no side, which is being unbiased or fair.

clue.text: An entire international decree

parts.note: an act is a law or decree passed by a parliament

explanation.surface: A complete worldwide ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entire is whole and undamaged, with nothing missing.

clue.text: It curdles, so get money back

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word for money from right to left

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note, British slang for money

explanation.surface: Something sours milk, so recover the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is British slang for a ten-pound note; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This enzyme preparation from calves' stomachs makes milk separate into curds and whey in cheesemaking.

clue.text: Impatient, so not so much repose

parts.note: repose and rest both mean relaxation
less means a smaller amount, not so much

explanation.surface: Being short of sleep makes a person edgy.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the clue's reverse order: 'repose' gives the first half, 'not so much' the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless person is fidgety and unable to wait calmly, so eager and unsettled.

clue.text: Lacking endorsements for secluded retreats

parts.note: lacking something means having no such thing
OKs are approvals or endorsements

explanation.surface: Hideaways that nobody has approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Corners and quiet recesses are cosy, sheltered hiding places.

clue.text: Three points to study at church, so settle comfortably

parts.note: E, N and S are three points of the compass, east, north and south
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone studies navigation in church, then makes themselves at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are a crossword staple for N, S, E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: To install oneself snugly somewhere is to get cosy in a safe spot.

clue.text: Telling off when you hit Chinese porcelain

parts.note: to slam is to strike hard
Ming porcelain dates from China's Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A scolding for whoever breaks a priceless vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Slamming in the informal sense is harsh criticism, a scolding or rebuke.

clue.text: In the soup, see? Maybe take partner

indicators.note: Maybe hints that the words soup and see could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Being in trouble might prompt someone to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble; 'Maybe' rearranges SOUP and SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed someone is to take them as a spouse, a husband or wife.

clue.text: Aid given back in first Asian country

indicators.note: first places the little word in at the front of the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: given back means the word aid is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Aid is returned to the leading nation of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given back' turns AID into DIA; 'first' puts IN before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The subcontinent nation with capital New Delhi lies in South Asia.

clue.text: Crash in mountain pass — lion is injured

parts.note: a col is a gap or pass between peaks

indicators.note: injured suggests damage, so the words lion is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lion is hurt in an accident high in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges LIONIS into LISION after COL.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash or impact between vehicles is an accident where they strike each other.

clue.text: Love the queen above all

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Romance and the monarch matter most of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the poetic contraction of 'over', meaning above.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic contraction of over, as in 'o'er the hills', means higher than.

clue.text: Think well, pal — correct the contents

indicators.note: the contents signals that the word for correct goes inside the word for pal

parts.note: a mate is a pal or friend
to edit is to correct text

explanation.surface: A friend is urged to revise the text of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the contents' puts EDIT inside MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect or ponder deeply.

clue.text: Hit by lorry after pubs close

indicators.note: after says the vehicle comes behind the letter taken from pubs
close means the end, so the final letter of pubs

parts.note: a truck is a lorry, the British word for a heavy goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked down by a lorry at closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' means the end of 'pubs', S; 'after' puts TRUCK behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past tense of strike, meaning hit or knocked.

clue.text: Taunt lara by displaying horribly hairy spider

indicators.note: horribly suggests a mess, so the letters of taunt lara are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone frightens Lara with a big ugly arachnid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges the nine letters of 'Taunt lara'.
explanation.definitionFit: The large furry tropical arachnid is famous for its fearsome look.

clue.text: Flower carried by a beast to backward 17

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden

indicators.note: backward tells you to read the solution to clue 17 in reverse

parts.note: the answer to 17 Across, meaning to trouble or distress

explanation.surface: A bloom is carried on an animal's back, heading off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns AIL, the answer to 17, into LIA after CAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The evergreen shrub with glossy leaves bears rose-like blooms.

clue.text: Failing to begin boat-trip may distress

indicators.note: failing to begin means the opening letter of the word is dropped; the run of letters inside Failing is a coincidence

parts.note: a sail is an outing in a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A voyage that never gets going could be upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to begin' removes the S from SAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, causing pain or worry.

clue.text: Did it again — it took an age for Edward

parts.note: taken as written
an era is an age or period
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: It took forever because Edward repeated things.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat, so iterated means repeated.

clue.text: When one iconoclastic king of Judah …

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
a means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: Starts a sentence about a Biblical monarch smashing idols, ellipsis carrying on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible says King Asa removed the idols and cut down his grandmother's image, so iconoclastic fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The third ruler of Judah's kingdom destroyed idols and pagan shrines according to the Books of Kings.

clue.text: … Is seen at the centre of a rock

definitions.text: … Is seen at the centre of a rock

parts.words: … Is seen at the centre of a rock
parts.note: continuing the previous clue, the king named there is found in the middle of a kind of stone

explanation.surface: Concludes the previous clue: the Judean king turns up in the heart of a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 19 sits in the middle of this answer, flanked by B and LT, which no clue word gives; the clue only defines the volcanic rock and points to where the king's name lies.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark, fine-grained volcanic stone forms from cooled lava, as at the Giant's Causeway.

clue.text: Write of prison

definitions.meaning: an enclosure, and slang for a jail

explanation.definitionFit: To pen a letter is to write it; a pen is also a confinement, as in the US slang for penitentiary.

clue.text: Acts to keep mushroom one receives

indicators.note: to keep means the word acts holds the mushroom inside it

parts.note: a cep is a porcini mushroom

explanation.surface: Someone takes in performances while holding a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts CEP inside ACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to take it when offered.

clue.text: Ain't case out at ranch

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are scattered, so ain't case is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone denies there is a case to answer out on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the eight letters of 'Ain't case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American cattle estate is a large farm.

clue.text: When on the road, wet weather causes tensions

definitions.note: the clue's plural stands for the uncountable sense of the answer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Rain on a journey frays tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just joins RAIN to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is pressure or stress, the stretched state that tension describes.

clue.text: Fleet can equip woman with weapon

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman can be given a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with weapon' rounds out the surface and hints at the arming.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of warships, like the Spanish one of 1588, is a navy fleet.

clue.text: Hindrance to détente negotiated about two kings

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the two kings
negotiated suggests something worked over, so the letters of détente are reworked

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, king, so two kings give two Rs

explanation.surface: Two monarchs agree a peace deal that turns out to be a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' rearranges DETENTE into DETEENT; 'about' sets it round RR to make DETE-RR-ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deterrent is something that discourages action, an obstacle.

clue.text: Heating measure in another module

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words another module

explanation.surface: A heating unit is covered in a separate course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters running through 'another module'.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used to bill gas supply in Britain.

clue.text: Mollify distressed, pale cat

indicators.note: distressed suggests disorder, so the letters of pale cat are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone soothes an anxious, ashen cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' rearranges the letters of 'pale cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to calm or pacify them.

clue.text: I'll take note in bad debt for quartered soldiers

indicators.note: in signals that the pair of pieces go inside the rearranged debt
bad suggests something spoiled, so debt is rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is dropped, leaving the letters as written
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone takes a note in a bad loan to house troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges DEBT into BTED; 'in' puts ILL+E inside after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops lodged in civilian homes are housed or accommodated there.
